newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador to reduce debt via smaller bond rollover.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador to reduce debt via smaller bond rollover.

text.p: Ecuador's government will reduce its internal debt this year by rolling over 20 percent less of the amount of bonds coming due this year, a government official said Friday.

"What is planned is to issue short-term bonds denominated in dollars making up 20 percent less of the maturing issue and to absorb the debt of sucre bonds and constant value units (UVCs)," an official from the Finance Ministry told Reuters.
"This forms part of the policy of reducing the internal debt burden," the official added.
Constant value units are a unit used in Ecuador, which are adjusted for changes in inflation.
In 1996, the government issued $240 million worth of bonds with maturities of less than a year, of which only $182.4 million will be rolled over.
So far in 1997, $88 million of bonds have been issued, leaving $94.4 million still to be placed. The bonds are issued only in Ecuador.
The official explained that the rollovers have to represent 20 percent less each year than the amounts placed in the previous year.
